datasets.label: cyclic_3d (point cloud, 3D)
datasets.text: Six peaks in a ring; the answer is a 6-cycle.

datasets.label: cyclic_10d (point cloud, 10D)
datasets.text: The same ring hidden in 10 dimensions.

datasets.label: ext_10d (point cloud, 10D)
datasets.text: Many bumps in 10D; most saddles close loops.

datasets.label: volcano_intact (paper Fig. 5, 2D)
datasets.text: Crater with 6 hills on its rim; every rim saddle is a ridge, so the spine is a ring.

datasets.label: volcano_notched (paper Fig. 5, 2D)
datasets.text: One rim saddle (30°) notched but still closer to the hills than to the crater floor: the paper keeps the ring. A p_hi below 0.28 wrongly opens it.

datasets.label: volcano_breached (paper Fig. 5, 2D)
datasets.text: The rim is breached at 30°, almost down to the crater floor: the paper cuts that saddle and the ring becomes a chain. Ours still draws a ring until p_hi is set below 0.51 (try 0.3).

datasets.label: fuel (volume 64³)
datasets.text: A jet: one elongated structure with a few maxima.

datasets.label: neghip (volume 64³)
datasets.text: Electron density around a protein: mirror-symmetric blobs.

datasets.label: silicium (volume 98x34x34)
datasets.text: One peak per atom on a lattice; mostly loops.
